questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : Data fragmentation increases as the depth of the decision tree increases.
S2 : Excessive data fragmentation can lead to overfitting in decision trees.
Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
(c)
• In a decision tree, each internal node splits data based on a threshold. As the tree grows
deeper, data is split into smaller subsets at each level. This is called data fragmentation -
fewer data points per node. Deeper trees mean more fragmentation. So, S1 is correct.
• When data becomes highly fragmented, nodes contain very few samples. The tree may then
fit noise instead of patterns, leading to overfitting and poor generalization. So S2 is correct.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : In agglomerative hierarchical clustering, the process starts with each data point as a separate cluster and merges the closest pairs iteratively.
S2 : In divisive hierarchical clustering, the algorithm starts with all data points in a single cluster and recursively splits it into smaller clusters.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• Agglomerative hierarchical clustering is a bottom-up approach where the algorithm starts
with each data point as an individual cluster and merges the closest pairs step by step until all
points are grouped into one cluster or the desired number of clusters is reached. So S1 is correct.
• Divisive hierarchical clustering is a top-down approach, beginning with all data points in a
single cluster, and then recursively splitting it into smaller, more refined clusters based on
dissimilarity measures. So, S2 is correct.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : A model with low bias and low variance is ideal but hard to achieve in practice.
S2 : Reducing variance often requires increasing bias slightly, which is the essence of the tradeoff.
Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
(c)
• In the best-performing model is one with both low bias (accurate predictions) and low variance (stable predictions). But in practice, such a model is hard to achieve due to the nature of realworld data and finite sample sizes. So, S1 is correct.
• The bias-variance tradeoff means that reducing one often increases the other. To reduce variance (i.e., overfitting), we usually simplify the model, which slightly increases bias-this tradeoff is fundamental in machine learning. So S2 is correct.

support vectors, meaning no data points are within or on the margin boundaries. So, S2 is

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: ReLU activation suffers from vanishing gradient problem.
LDA is not applicable when the classes have unequal covariance matrices.
The bias-variance trade-off shows that both high bias and high variance can lead to high test error.

questions.solution:
(d)
• ReLU helps to reduce to vanishing gradient problem. Change it may case dead neuron. So
option (a) is correct.
• LDA assumes equal covariance for all classes. If the covariance matrices are unequal, the
assumption is violated, and LDA may perform poorly. In such cases, Quadratic Discriminant
Analysis (QDA) is more appropriate. So, option (b) is correct.
• This is a foundational concept in learning theory.
High bias → underfitting → poor performance
High variance → overfitting → poor generalization
The total test error is minimized by balancing the two. So, option (c) is correct.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

options.text: Multicollinearity is reduced as the number of dimensions increases.
Redundant or correlated features make interpretation harder in high-dimensional data.
Dimensionality reduction increases the number of irrelevant features.

questions.solution:
(b)
• Multicollinearity typically increases in high-dimensional spaces because adding more features
increases the chance of correlation between them. So, option (a) is incorrect.
• Redundant or correlated features (which are common in high-dimensional data) make models
harder to interpret, especially in linear models where understanding individual feature effects
is important. So, option (b) is correct.
• Dimensionality reduction techniques like PCA or LDA are designed to remove irrelevant or
redundant features, not increase them. So, option (c) is incorrect.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : LDA assumes that each class has a Gaussian distribution with a shared covariance matrix.
S2 : LDA always results in nonlinear decision boundaries between the classes.
S3 : Naive Bayes classification assumes that the features are independent within each class.
Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
(b)
• Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) is based on the assumption that:
(i) Each class follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution, and
(ii) All classes share the same covariance matrix (homoscedasticity). So, S1 is correct.
• This assumption allows LDA to derive linear decision boundaries analytically.
• LDA produces linear decision boundaries in the input feature space.
• These boundaries are based on solving a linear equation involving the inverse of the shared
covariance matrix and class means.
• Non-linear boundaries may occur in Kernel LDA, but not in standard LDA. So, S2 is incorrect.
• This is the central assumption of Naive Bayes: given the class label, the features are assumed
to be conditionally independent.
• This assumption simplifies the joint likelihood into a product of individual feature likelihoods.
So, S3 is correct.

S1 : The approximation error of a polynomial regression model depends on the number of training points.
S2 : The structural error of a polynomial regression model depends on the number of training point.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• As the number of training points increases, the fitted polynomial can match the underlying function more closely within the same model class, so the approximation improves. So, S1 is correct.
• Structural error is related to limitations of the model’s capacity (like fixed polynomial degree) and stays constant regardless of how many data points are used. So S2 is correct.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: In K-Fold Cross Validation, the number of models trained equals the number of folds used.
A larger K generally leads to higher bias but lower computational cost.
Leave-One-Out Cross Validation tends to have lower variance compared to lower K-fold values.

questions.solution:
(a)
• In K-Fold Cross Validation, the dataset is divided into K folds, and the model is trained K times, each time using a different fold as the test set. So, the number of models trained equals the number of folds. So, option (a) is correct.
• A larger K usually leads to lower bias but higher computational cost (opposite of what is stated). So, option (b) is incorrect.
• Leave-One-Out Cross Validation (LOOCV), which is the case where K = n typically has higher
variance, not lower. So, option (c) is incorrect.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: The dropout technique is used to prevent overfitting in neural networks.
A confusion matrix is used to evaluate the performance of classification models.
Cross-entropy loss is used to measure regression accuracy.
The Learning rate represents the step size in the gradient descent algorithm.

questions.solution:
(a, b, d)
• Dropout is a regularization method where randomly selected neurons are ignored during
training. This helps the model generalize better and prevents overfitting. So, option (a) is
correct.
• A confusion matrix is a table used to measure the performance of a classification algorithm. It
includes values like True Positives, False Positives, True Negatives, and False Negatives.
From this, metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score can be calculated. So, option (b)
is correct.
• Cross-Entropy Loss is used for classification problems, not regression. For regression tasks,
common loss functions include Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE).
So, option (c) is incorrect.
• The learning rate controls how much the model's weights are updated during each step of
optimization. A higher learning rate might speed up training but can overshoot the minimum,
while a smaller learning rate might take more time but converge smoothly. So, option (d) is
correct.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: A decision tree selects thresholds that maximize class impurity after each split.
A decision tree selects the threshold at each node by minimizing information gain.
A decision tree selects the threshold at each node by maximizing information gain.

questions.solution:
(c)
• Decision trees aim to reduce impurity, not increase it. After each split, they try to make child
nodes more pure (homogeneous). So, option (a) is incorrect.
• Information gain represents the reduction in impurity after a split. The tree chooses the
threshold that maximizes this value, not minimizes it. So, option (b) is incorrect.
• A decision tree selects the threshold that results in the highest information gain among all
candidates. This helps create the most informative split. So, option (c) is correct.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: Ridge regression is a regularization technique that uses L1 penalty to reduce overfitting.
Ridge regression does not help in correcting multicollinearity in linear regression models.
Ridge regression penalizes large model coefficients using L2 regularization.
Ridge regression can also be applied to logistic regression models.

questions.solution:
(c, d)
• Ridge regression uses L2 regularization, not L1. The L1 penalty is used in Lasso Regression,
which promotes sparsity in the coefficients. So, option (a) is incorrect.
• Multicollinearity-a condition where predictor variables are highly correlated. It does so by
adding a penalty term to shrink coefficients, thus stabilizing estimates. So, option (b) is incorrect.
• Ridge regression introduces a penalty equal to the square of the magnitude of coefficients (L2
norm). This discourages large coefficients and helps reduce overfitting. So, option (c) is correct.
• Although Ridge regression is mainly introduced in the context of linear regression, it can also
be extended to logistic regression for classification problems by applying the L2 penalty to
the cost function. So, option (d) is correct.

Normalized margin is used to improve classification accuracy.
Normalized margin is undefined for nonlinear classifiers.

questions.solution:
(a)
Raw margin can be arbitrarily increased by scaling the feature vectors. Normalized margin divides
by the weight vector norm to give a meaningful, scale-invariant measure for generalization.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: LDA minimizes the distance between the means of different classes.
LDA minimizes the variance within each class.
LDA can be applied always when only one class is present in the dataset.
LDA may not perform well when the number of features exceeds the number of samples.

questions.solution:
(b, d)
• LDA aims to maximize the between-class scatter, which involves increasing the distance between
the class means to enhance class separability. So, option (a) is incorrect.
• Minimizing the distance between class means would reduce class separability, which goes
against the fundamental purpose of LDA.
• One of the objectives of LDA is to minimize the within-class scatter (i.e., variance within the
same class), so that samples from the same class are grouped closely together after projection.
• This helps in achieving better class separation in the transformed space. So, option (b) is
correct.
• LDA is a supervised classification method that relies on comparing multiple classes.
• When only one class is present, there is no between-class information to learn from, so LDA
cannot be applied in such cases. So, option (c) is incorrect.
• When the number of features (dimensions) is greater than the number of training samples,
the within-class scatter matrix becomes singular (non-invertible).
• This causes numerical instability and can degrade LDA's performance unless modifications or
regularization techniques are applied. So, option (d) is correct.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a linear technique that projects data onto directions of maximum variance.
t-SNE is a non-linear technique that preserves local neighborhood structure in high-dimensional data.
Dimensionality reduction helps in mitigating the curse of dimensionality and improves model interpretability.
In PCA, the principal components are chosen based on the minimum variance in the data.

questions.solution:
(a, b, c)
• PCA is a linear dimensionality reduction technique that projects the data onto orthogonal
directions (principal components) that capture the maximum variance in the dataset.
So, option (a) is correct.
• t-SNE (t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding) is a non-linear method that is especially
effective for visualizing high-dimensional data, as it focuses on preserving local neighborhood
relationships. So, option (b) is correct.
• Dimensionality reduction reduces the number of features, which helps in reducing
computational cost, overfitting, and improving interpretability, especially in high-dimensional
settings - thus helping to mitigate the curse of dimensionality. So, option (c) is correct.
• PCA selects principal components based on maximum, not minimum, variance. The first principal
component captures the largest variance, the second captures the next highest, and so on. So,
option (d) is incorrect.
